verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and complete. In the forward implication, vertices along any cycle alternate between the two bipartition classes, forcing the cycle length to be even. In the converse implication, parity of shortest-path distance from a root in each connected component partitions the vertices; if an edge joined two vertices of the same parity, the two shortest paths together with that edge would form an odd closed walk. The cited signed predecessor fact ec5be0d896864f8c states exactly that every odd closed walk in a finite undirected graph contains an odd cycle, yielding the required contradiction. The cited fact has a self-contained unconditional statement and does not trigger the P3 chain prohibition. The candidate statement is self-contained, no hard prohibition is violated, and there are no external-paper references requiring retrieval.
